sections.heading: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines

questions.q: In triangle $ABC$, $a=9$, $b=12$, and angle $C=55^\circ$. Find side $c$, to the nearest tenth, using the Law of Cosines.
In triangle $ABC$, angle $A=40^\circ$, angle $B=70^\circ$, and $a=8$. Find side $b$, to the nearest tenth, using the Law of Sines.
In triangle $ABC$, $a=7$, $b=10$, $c=13$. Find the largest angle, to the nearest degree, using the Law of Cosines.
questions.answer: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, so we find angle $C$: $\cos C=\dfrac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2ab}=\dfrac{49+100-169}{2(7)(10)}=\dfrac{-20}{140}\approx-0.1429$. $C=\cos^{-1}(-0.1429)\approx98^\circ$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: the height of a lighthouse

questions.q: This question has two parts. A ship observes a lighthouse at an angle of elevation of $18^\circ$. After sailing 500 meters directly toward the lighthouse, the angle of elevation increases to $30^\circ$. (a) Let $h$ be the lighthouse's height and $d$ the final distance from its base. Write two equations relating $h$ and $d$ using the tangent ratio. (b) Solve the system to find $h$, to the nearest meter.
questions.answer: (a) At the closer position: $\tan(30^\circ)=\dfrac{h}{d}$, so $h=d\tan(30^\circ)$. At the farther position (distance $d+500$): $\tan(18^\circ)=\dfrac{h}{d+500}$, so $h=(d+500)\tan(18^\circ)$. (b) Setting equal: $d\tan(30^\circ)=(d+500)\tan(18^\circ)$. Using $\tan(30^\circ)\approx0.5774$ and $\tan(18^\circ)\approx0.3249$: $0.5774d=0.3249d+162.45$, so $0.2525d=162.45$, giving $d\approx643.4$. Then $h=643.4\times0.5774\approx372$ meters.
